drivers.name: Hisense VIDAA TV
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Hisense VIDAA OS TVs over the TV's embedded MQTT broker (the path the RemoteNOW/VIDAA app uses). Power, volume, input, key passthrough, and PIN pairing.

help.overview:
Hisense VIDAA TVs are controlled over an MQTT broker built into the TV (port 36669), the same way the RemoteNOW phone app works. Enter the TV's IP address, then pair: run 'Request Pairing' (a 4-digit PIN appears on the TV), then 'Submit Pairing PIN' with that number. The pairing is remembered across restarts.

Power On over the network is best-effort: a TV in deep standby turns its broker off, so it may be unreachable until switched on with the physical remote. Power Off and everything else work while the TV is on.
help.setup:
1. Make sure the TV and OpenAVC are on the same network.
2. On the TV, enable mobile-app/remote control if it has such a setting (Settings > System > Mobile App / 'RemoteNOW').
3. Enter the TV's IP address and save.
4. Run 'Request Pairing', read the PIN on the TV, then run 'Submit Pairing PIN'.

Client certificate (only if pairing/connection fails): some newer models require a client certificate for the TLS connection. OpenAVC does not ship it. If the device stays offline with a TLS error, obtain the VIDAA app client certificate and key (the community publishes them, e.g. github.com/tombabolewski/vidaa-control) and paste them into the 'Client Certificate (PEM)' and 'Client Key (PEM)' fields below.

drivers.name: Kramer Protocol 3000
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Kramer products via Protocol 3000 over TCP (port 5000) or RS-232. Covers matrix switchers (VS series), scalers and presentation switchers (VP series), and distribution amplifiers. On matrix models each configured output and input is a child entity with per-output routing, mute, volume, and sink state. Routing commands speak both Protocol 3000 routing dialects (legacy VID/AUD/AV and layer-based ROUTE), so one driver covers the whole family.

help.overview: Controls Kramer matrix switchers, scalers, presentation switchers, and distribution amplifiers via Protocol 3000. Common in corporate AV, education, and houses of worship. On matrix switchers, configure the frame size (Input Count / Output Count) and every output becomes a child entity tracking its routed input, mutes, volume, and connected sink, with per-input signal and HDCP detection. Front-panel switches are pushed by the device and reflected immediately.
help.setup: 1. Connect the switcher to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the IP address via the front panel menu or Kramer Network. 3. Enter the IP address and port 5000 (default) in the device config. 4. Matrix switchers: set Input Count and Output Count to the frame size (e.g. 8 and 8 for a VS-88H2). Each output and input becomes a child entity. Leave both at 0 for single-output devices (scalers, presentation switchers, DAs). 5. Machine number defaults to 01. Change it if multiple daisy-chained Kramer units share one serial line. 6. If the device supports Protocol 3000 security (#SECUR), leave it disabled — the driver does not send #LOGIN.

models: VP Series scalers and presentation switchers
compatible_models.notes: Any Kramer product implementing Protocol 3000. For matrix switchers, set Input Count / Output Count to the frame size to get per-output routing and mute state; leave both 0 for single-output devices. VS-series HDMI matrices use the legacy VID/AUD/AV routing dialect, VP-series scalers the layer-based ROUTE dialect — the driver's routing commands send both forms, and the unsupported one answers a benign error. Device security (#SECUR), where present, must be left disabled.

drivers.name: LG SICP Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls LG commercial displays via SICP over TCP (port 9761). Each Set ID on an RS-232 daisy chain is a display child entity with power, input, volume, mute, screen-off, signal status, picture settings, and panel health. Covers webOS Signage, LED, and OLED commercial series.

help.overview: Controls LG commercial displays using the SICP protocol. One connection can address several displays daisy-chained over RS-232 by Set ID — each appears as a display child entity with power, input, volume, mute, screen blank, signal status, picture settings, and panel health.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display (or the chain's first display) to the network.
2. Default control port is 9761.
3. In each display's OSD (Settings > General), give it a unique Set ID. List those IDs in 'Display Set IDs' — e.g. 1 for a single display, or 1,2,3,4 for a daisy-chained video wall. Enter the IDs exactly as the OSD shows them (decimal); the driver handles the protocol's hex encoding.
4. Route commands to a display by picking it from the Display dropdown; use All Displays On / Off to drive the whole chain at once.

drivers.name: LG WebOS
drivers.author: Keaton Stacks
drivers.description: Controls LG WebOS TVs (2016+) via the SSAP WebSocket protocol.

help.overview: Controls LG WebOS televisions using the SSAP protocol over a secure WebSocket connection on port 3001.  Supports power, volume, input switching, and app launching.
help.setup: Enable 'LG Connect Apps' or network control in the TV's General settings. A pairing prompt will appear on the TV screen on first connect. If the prompt does not appear, use the 'Force Pair' command.

drivers.name: Lightware LW3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lightware switchers and matrix routers via Protocol #3 (LW3) over TCP port 6107. Covers UCX, Taurus UCX, MMX2, MMX, and MX2M products. Each configured output and input is a child entity tracking its routed source, mute, lock, HDCP, 5V and signal-type state per port, updated in real time via change-notification subscriptions with a keep-alive watchdog guarding the link. Provides video and audio crosspoint switching, EDID switching, analog audio level/mute/balance, and CEC command sending.

help.overview: Lightware LW3 is the unified ASCII control protocol used across Lightware's matrix switchers, extenders, and modular routers. Commands target a tree of nodes (e.g. /V1/MEDIA/VIDEO/XP) using GET, SET, and CALL operations. The driver exposes the most-used runtime control surface: video and audio routing, mute, HDCP, output power, EDID, analog audio level, and CEC.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Lightware device to the network via Ethernet. 2. Confirm the device's IP address using LDC (Lightware Device Controller)
   or the front-panel display.
3. In LDC's Network tab, ensure the LW3 service on port 6107 is enabled
   and that authentication (IPLogin) is OFF — this driver does not
   authenticate.
4. Enter the IP address and port 6107 in the device config. 5. Set Input Count and Output Count to the frame size (default 4/4
   covers UCX, Taurus, and MMX2) — each port becomes a child entity
   with per-port routing, mute, lock, HDCP, 5V and signal state.
6. Use input/output port numbers as integers (I3 → input=3, O2 → output=2).
   Setting input=0 disconnects an output.

compatible_models.notes: Any Lightware product that implements LW3 (most products since 2012). Set Input Count / Output Count to the frame size — each port becomes a child entity with per-port state (default 4/4 covers UCX, Taurus, and MMX2). Commands accept any port number regardless; ports a model doesn't have answer LW3 errors on poll, which is benign.

drivers.name: Lutron HomeWorks QS
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lutron HomeWorks QS Processors (HQP6-2, HQP7) over Telnet using the Lutron Integration Protocol (LIP). Supports zone level control (OUTPUT), keypad/phantom button presses and LED control (DEVICE), area occupancy queries (AREA), and shade group control (SHADEGRP). Use phantom keypad button presses to activate scenes.

help.overview: Lutron HomeWorks QS is a residential and small-commercial lighting, shade, and HVAC control system. The HomeWorks QS Processor exposes a Telnet integration protocol (LIP) on port 23 that lets external controllers raise/lower lights and shades, press phantom keypad buttons (which activate scenes programmed in the Lutron design software), and monitor occupancy.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the HomeWorks QS Processor's IP address (set a static
   reservation on the network).
2. In the HomeWorks QS Design software, on the Integration tab,
   assign Integration IDs to the outputs, devices (keypads), areas,
   and shade groups you want to control. Note them down — you'll
   reference them in macros and triggers.
3. Confirm a Telnet login exists for integration use. Defaults are
   "lutron" / "integration" but the integrator may have changed
   them in the design software. Enter the username and password
   in the device config below.
4. To activate a scene: program a phantom keypad in the design
   software, assign each button to a scene, then use the
   "Press Button" command with that keypad's Integration ID and
   the button's Component Number.
5. Zone (OUTPUT) levels are 0-100 percent. Fade and Delay times
   are optional and accept SS.ss, SS, MM:SS, or HH:MM:SS formats.

compatible_models.notes: HomeWorks QS Processor (HQP6-2 and HQP7). Other Lutron systems (RadioRA 3, Caseta SB Pro, Athena, QS Standalone) speak related but distinct protocol surfaces and are not covered by this driver.

drivers.name: Mersive Solstice Pod
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Mersive Solstice Pods (and Solstice Windows Software) over the OpenControl REST API. Boot users, clear posts, suspend and wake the display, reset the on-screen key, push bulletin or emergency banners, and monitor connected users and post counts.

help.overview:
Mersive Solstice is a wireless presentation system. Users share screens, video, and media from laptops, phones, and tablets to a Solstice Pod that drives the room display.

OpenAVC controls the Pod's runtime: clear posts, boot all users at end-of-meeting, sleep / wake the display, reset the on-screen connection key, and push bulletin or emergency banners. Live state includes connected users, active posts, bandwidth, and the current screen key.

Install-time configuration (network setup, calendar integration, splash-screen images) stays in the Solstice Dashboard. RS-232 pass-thru is exposed for chained-display control via a USB-to-serial adapter on the Pod.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the Pod has Solstice Enterprise Edition. The OpenControl API is gated to Enterprise hosts.
2. In the Solstice Dashboard, set an admin password (strongly recommended — without one, any device on the network can drive this Pod).
3. Enter the Pod's IP address and admin password here. Default port is 80 (HTTP). Tick Use HTTPS for port 443; Solstice ships with a self-signed certificate which the driver does not verify.
4. Mersive recommends polling no more than once every 10 seconds. The default interval is 30 s; the minimum is 10 s.

compatible_models.notes: Requires Solstice Enterprise Edition license — Standard Edition Pods do not expose the OpenControl API. Some commands are Pod-only (reboot, hardware variant, HDMI input force-off); Windows Software hosts ignore them. Power-management / suspend / wake are Pod-only.

drivers.name: Middle Atlantic RackLink PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Middle Atlantic / Legrand RackLink RLNK power distribution units (Select, Premium, Premium+) over the RackLink Control Protocol on TCP port 60000. Outlet and dry-contact control, sequencing, naming, EPO, and live voltage / current / temperature / wattage telemetry. Premium models push unsolicited status changes; Select models fall back to polling.

help.overview: RackLink is the Middle Atlantic (now Legrand AV) family of network-controlled rack PDUs commonly installed in commercial AV racks. The driver speaks the binary RackLink Control Protocol so macros can switch outlets on / off, cycle outlets to power-cycle frozen gear, sequence the rack up / down, and (on Premium / Premium+ units) read live telemetry.
help.setup:
1. Connect the PDU to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the PDU's IP from the RackLink front panel or web UI.
3. Log into the PDU's web UI as Administrator and set the passwords for Administrator, User, and Control Systems accounts. The control protocol is disabled until those passwords are set.
4. On Premium+ models, enable the control protocol under Device Settings → Network Services → Control Protocol, and enter a username for an admin account that has the control protocol enabled.
5. Enter the IP, port 60000, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC. Default Select / Premium credentials are user / password (whatever was set in step 3).

compatible_models.notes: All RackLink series share the Control Protocol on TCP 60000. Select models support outlet control, naming, sequencing, and dry contacts. Premium and Premium+ add per-system telemetry (voltage, current, wattage, temperature, surge state, occupancy), EPO, and pushed status updates.

drivers.name: NETGEAR M4250 / M4350 AV Line Switch
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Monitor and control NETGEAR M4250 and M4350 AV Line managed switches over their CLI: per-port PoE power-cycling and draw, link state, multicast/IGMP health, system health (temperature, fans, PSU, CPU), reboot, and config save. Each port is a child entity.

help.overview: Controls a NETGEAR M4250 or M4350 AV Line managed switch. Add it as one device; every physical port appears as a child entity under the Child Entities tab with its link state, PoE draw, and connected device. The driver auto-detects which family you have.
help.setup:
New switches ship with SSH turned off, so turn it on before you add the switch here.
1. Reach the switch. It asks for an IP by DHCP and falls back to 169.254.100.100 if no DHCP server answers. Open its web UI (or a console session). You are prompted to change the default admin password on first login.
2. Enable SSH: System > Management Access in the web UI, or run 'ip ssh server enable' in the CLI. SSH is the secure transport this driver uses.
3. Choose auth. Key auth is recommended: set Auth Method to 'key' and install the OpenAVC public key on the switch. Otherwise set Auth Method to 'password' and enter the admin password.
4. Add it here: enter the switch IP and the admin username (default 'admin'); leave the port at 22.
5. If the admin account lands in User EXEC mode, set the Enable Password so the driver can enter Privileged EXEC.
6. Ports, PoE status, and connected devices are discovered automatically once it connects.
help.connection: This switch ships with SSH turned off, so a brand-new switch can't connect until SSH is enabled on it. Use the Enable SSH button below to do that automatically — it connects over telnet, enables SSH, saves, and switches this device to SSH. Or enable it by hand (switch web UI, System > Management Access, or 'ip ssh server enable' in the CLI), then check the IP, the admin username (default 'admin'), and the password.

compatible_models.notes: Validated against an M4250-40G8XF-PoE+ (software 13.0.5.14): PoE draw/control, ports, IGMP/multicast, system health, config save, and reboot exercised on hardware.
Shares the CLI per the M4250/M4350 CLI Reference Manual; not yet validated on M4350 hardware.

drivers.name: Novastar H Series Video Wall Splicer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Novastar H series video wall splicers via UDP JSON commands. Covers layer operations, preset management, input switching, brightness, fade-to-black, freeze, volume, test patterns, screen color, OSD, and device management. Compatible with H2, H5, H9, H15, H20, and similar models using the H Series Control Protocol.

help.overview: Controls Novastar H series LED video wall splicers. These processors manage LED wall layouts, input routing, presets, and screen settings. Common in large-format LED installations including houses of worship, corporate lobbies, broadcast studios, and live event stages.
help.setup:
1. Connect the processor to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the processor's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 3. Enter the IP address and port 6000 (default) in the device config. 4. Device ID defaults to 0. If using multiple processors, set the
   device_id config field to match each unit's ID.
5. Screen ID defaults to 0. Set screen_id for multi-screen setups.

drivers.name: ONVIF Camera (discovery)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Discovery-only anchor for cameras and AV devices that answer the ONVIF WS-Discovery multicast probe. Surfaces manufacturer, hardware model, and ONVIF service URLs in scan results so vendor-specific camera drivers can claim the device as primary; otherwise the user gets a placeholder they can swap for a control driver later.

help.overview: ONVIF cameras advertise themselves on the local network via SOAP-over-UDP WS-Discovery (multicast group 239.255.255.250 port 3702). A scan listens for ProbeMatch responses and reads each camera's manufacturer + hardware fields from the scope URIs so the matcher can identify the device. Use this anchor when no vendor-specific driver is available; replace it with the vendor's control driver once one ships in the catalog.
help.setup:
1. Run a network scan from the discovery panel. 2. ONVIF cameras that answer the multicast Probe surface with
   manufacturer, hardware model, and ONVIF service URLs read from
   their scope URIs.
3. If a vendor-specific camera driver matches the device's
   manufacturer or OUI, that driver wins primary identification
   and this anchor demotes to an alternative.
4. If no specific driver matches, add this anchor — you'll get
   a placeholder device entry surfacing the camera's identity.
   Install / build the right control driver next and swap it in.

models: Any IP camera or AV device that answers ONVIF WS-Discovery with a NetworkVideoTransmitter scope (Axis, Hanwha, Hikvision, Bosch, Sony, Panasonic, AVer, Vaddio, PTZOptics, Lumens, Marshall, etc.)
compatible_models.notes: Discovery-only entry. Tested against the ONVIF Network Specification §7 scope URI format; firmware variations in the SOAP envelope are tolerated. For control, use the matching vendor-specific camera driver once it ships in the catalog.

drivers.name: Panasonic AW-HE/UE/UN PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic AW-HE, AW-UE, and AW-UN series professional PTZ cameras via the documented HTTP CGI protocol (port 80). Covers power, pan/tilt drive and absolute positioning, zoom, focus (auto/manual), iris (auto/ manual), 100 presets, tally, wireless remote enable, and zoom-linked pan/tilt speed. Image-quality controls (gain, white balance, scene files, gamma) are install-time setup left to the camera's web UI.

help.overview: Panasonic AW-HE/UE/UN are professional PTZ cameras commonly used in broadcast, houses of worship, lecture capture, and corporate AV. The cameras are controlled over HTTP using a small CGI command set. This driver exposes the full pan/tilt/zoom/focus/iris/preset/tally surface needed for live room control. Image quality settings (color, gain, white balance, scene files) are configured in the camera's web UI.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the camera via its web UI (default credentials
   are typically admin / 12345 — change them).
2. Enter the camera's IP address below. Default port is 80. 3. If you've enabled HTTP authentication on the camera, set Auth Type
   to "basic" and enter the username and password.
4. Pan/tilt drive uses speed values 01..99 per axis (50 = stop, 50/50
   both stop). The home position is APC8000/8000.
5. Presets are numbered 1..100 in the UI; the protocol uses 0..99
   internally, but the driver exposes the 1..100 numbering.
6. Polling is set to 10 seconds by default. Keep this at or above 5 s
   — the cameras throttle aggressive polling and have a 130 ms minimum
   inter-command gap.

compatible_models.notes: Verified end to end on real hardware, including the iris position query (AW-HE145 firmware V01.28, AW-HE40 firmware V1.94).

All AW-HE / AW-UE / AW-UN PTZ models on firmware 4.x+. The AK-UB300 (box camera) is in the same protocol family but does not support most pan/tilt/zoom commands — it returns errors for unsupported operations which the driver simply ignores.

drivers.name: Panasonic PT-MZ / PT-RZ Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic PT-MZ (LCD) and PT-RZ (DLP) professional installation projectors via the NTCONTROL TCP protocol (Protocol 2). Power, input, shutter / AV mute, freeze, and operating-hours readout. Supports Panasonic's MD5 session-challenge authentication so the projector keeps its default Web Control admin password.

help.overview: Panasonic NTCONTROL (Protocol 2) is the TCP control channel shared across all Panasonic professional projectors. It runs on TCP 1024 by default with optional MD5 challenge-response authentication tied to the projector's Web Control admin account.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network and assign a static IP.
2. In the projector's main menu, set [Network] -> [Network Control] -> [Command Control] = ON. The default command port is 1024.
3. Open the projector's Web Control page in a browser. Set or change the Administrator-Authorized password (default username is ``admin1``, default password is ``panasonic``).
4. In OpenAVC, enter the projector's IP and the Web Control admin username and password. If you left the password blank in the projector's web UI (non-protected mode), leave the password field empty here too.

compatible_models.notes: Protocol 2 / NTCONTROL is the same on every Panasonic professional projector — the universal command surface (power, input select, shutter, freeze, operating hours) is consistent. Per-model variation is which physical inputs are present; the driver exposes the union and the projector returns ``ERR2`` for inputs it doesn't have, which the driver logs at debug.

drivers.name: Poly Studio (VideoOS)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Poly (HP) Studio X30, X50, X70, E70, and G7500 video collaboration bars via the public VideoOS REST API. Audio / video mute, volume, camera presets and direction nudges, hangup, reboot — everything needed to wire Poly bars into a touch panel.

help.overview: Poly VideoOS exposes a documented REST API on HTTPS 443 for control of audio mute, volume, privacy / video mute, camera control and presets, active call hangup, and system reboot. The driver uses session-cookie authentication — log in once with the device's admin credentials and the session is reused for the lifetime of the connection.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Poly bar to the network and assign a static IP.
2. From the bar's web UI (https://<ip>) sign in as Admin and confirm the API is enabled. The factory default password is the device's serial number on first boot — change it immediately to a site-specific password.
3. In OpenAVC, enter the bar's IP, the admin username (default ``admin``), and the password. Leave the port at 443.

compatible_models.notes: VideoOS REST API is identical across the X-series and G7500. Per-model differences (mic count, integrated cameras, bundled mic pods) don't change the command surface — they just gate which features actually do anything when invoked.

drivers.name: PTZOptics Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls PTZOptics PTZ cameras over the VISCA-over-IP protocol on TCP port 5678. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, preset recall / save / reset, tally light, image flip, auto-exposure mode, white balance mode, and backlight. Polled state covers pan / tilt / zoom / focus position, focus mode, AE mode, WB mode, backlight, and flip settings.

help.overview:
PTZOptics cameras are widely used in classrooms, houses of worship, and conference rooms. This driver speaks raw VISCA over TCP 5678 (no Sony VISCA-over-IP header), which is what PTZOptics cameras actually expose — UDP 1259 also works but TCP gives reliable delivery for absolute-position commands.

VISCA is request/response only. The driver polls the camera every few seconds for pan / tilt / zoom / focus position and exposure / WB state. Joystick-style movement uses pt_up / pt_down / etc. with pt_stop to halt; absolute moves use pt_absolute with explicit pan and tilt positions.
help.setup:
1. Find the camera's IP via the OSD menu, the PTZOptics utility, or your router's DHCP table.
2. Confirm VISCA-over-IP is enabled in the camera's web UI (Settings → Network or Settings → VISCA). Most cameras ship with it on by default.
3. Enter the IP in OpenAVC. Port 5678 is fixed.
4. After connecting, pan_position / tilt_position / zoom_position will populate automatically.
5. Save up to 128 presets (numbered 0–127). 'set preset speed' applies to subsequent recalls.

compatible_models.notes: All PTZOptics cameras share the same VISCA-over-IP command set on TCP 5678. Older models may not support every command (the camera ignores unknown ones). 12X-USB needs PTZOptics' IP/serial bridge for network control.

drivers.name: QSC Q-SYS QRC
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls QSC Q-SYS Cores via QRC (Q-SYS Remote Control) — JSON-RPC 2.0 over TCP port 1710. Auto-discovers the running design's Components and their controls on connect (no manual block list), models each Component as a typed child entity, and streams real-time state via Change Group auto-poll. Covers Component control, Named Controls, Mixer, Audio Router, Snapshot recall/save, Loop Player, and PA Router paging.

help.overview: Comprehensive QSC Q-SYS control over QRC (JSON-RPC 2.0 on TCP 1710). On connect the driver reads the running design's Components and their controls straight from the Core and lists each Component as a child entity under the device — no block list to type. Every control is subscribed via a Change Group with auto-poll, so bindings update in real time. Use the per-component commands (Set Gain, Set Mute, Mixer …, Recall Snapshot, …) in macros and panels, and 'Re-import Topology' after you change the Q-SYS design.
help.setup:
STEP 1 — Expose your blocks in Q-SYS Designer.
For each block you want to control (Gain, Mixer, Router, Snapshot Controller, Loop Player, …), open its Properties and set 'Script Access' to 'External' (or 'All'). Give it a clear 'Code Name'. Components WITHOUT Script Access = External are invisible to QRC — this is the #1 setup mistake. Save to Core & Run (F5) so the change takes effect.

STEP 2 — (Optional) Named Controls.
Individual controls you drag into Designer's Named Controls list (e.g. 'Volume', 'Mute') can be monitored too. QRC cannot enumerate these, so list any you want in the 'Named Controls' field below — one per line, optionally followed by a type (number/boolean/string/trigger). Most rooms need none, since Components are discovered automatically.

STEP 3 — Enter the Core's IP address above.
If the Core has authentication enabled (Core Manager → Users), fill in Username and Password; otherwise leave them blank.

STEP 4 — Save. Within a second or two the device connects, the Core's status (Active/Idle/Standby), model, design name, and health populate, and each exposed Component appears under the device's Components tab with its live, typed controls. Bind child state (e.g. device.<id>.component.PgmGain.gain) to UI elements, or drive commands like 'Set Gain' / 'Recall Snapshot' from macros and panel buttons.

Troubleshooting:
  • No components listed — the blocks aren't exposed. Set Script Access = External in Designer and redeploy (F5). Use the 'Test Connection' action to list what QRC currently sees.
  • 'Connection refused' on 1710 — the Core isn't in Run mode, or a VLAN ACL blocks QRC.
  • Logon errors — set Username/Password to match a Q-SYS user.
  • Design changed — run the 'Re-import Topology' action (or the Components tab's Refresh) to re-read the control surface.
  • Need something the typed commands don't cover — use 'Set Component Control' or 'Send Raw JSON-RPC'.

compatible_models.notes: Verified end-to-end against a live Core 24f: auto-discovery (Component.GetComponents / GetControls), change-group push, and round-trips for gain/mute, mixer crosspoint, router, snapshot, and Named Controls.

Every Q-SYS Core that runs Q-SYS Designer speaks QRC (TCP 1710) — the same protocol verified on the Core 24f — so these are expected to work but haven't been tested on real hardware. This driver uses QRC, not the legacy ECP (TCP 1702). In Designer, set each block's Script Access to External (or All) so it appears in auto-discovery; add Named Controls to the Named Controls list to monitor them.

drivers.name: Roku (ECP)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Roku streaming players and Roku TVs over the local network using the External Control Protocol (ECP). Full remote surface, text entry, app launch/install, and TV power, volume, input, and tuner control on supported models.

help.overview: Controls Roku streaming players and Roku TVs over the local network using Roku's External Control Protocol (ECP). Provides the full remote-control surface (navigation, transport, search, and on-screen text entry), app launch and install, and TV power, volume, input, and tuner control on supported models. Reports power state, the currently active app, and media playback status. No Roku account, PIN, or cloud connection is required, and it works with third-party Roku TVs too.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Roku to the same network and note its IP address (Settings > Network > About, or the Roku mobile app).
2. On the Roku, set Settings > System > Control by mobile apps > Network access to 'Default' or 'Permissive' (NOT 'Disabled'). Roku OS 14.1 and later block remote key presses when this is off; the driver then reports Mobile Control Enabled = false and key presses return HTTP 403.
3. Enter the IP address. The port is 8060 (do not change).
4. No PIN, password, or account is needed.
5. To launch an app, use Launch App with its channel ID. Find an installed app's ID by opening it and reading the Active App ID state, or browse http://<roku-ip>:8060/query/apps in a browser. Common IDs: Netflix 12, Amazon Prime Video 13.

compatible_models.notes: Any Roku device with 'Control by mobile apps' enabled, including third-party Roku TVs (TCL, Hisense, onn, etc.). Power, volume, and input/tuner keys apply to models that report supports-tv-power-control.

drivers.name: Samsung MDC Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Samsung commercial displays via the MDC (Multiple Display Control) binary protocol over TCP. Each Set ID on the chain is a display child entity with power, volume, mute, input, and picture settings (brightness, contrast, backlight, picture mode, color tone).

help.overview: Controls Samsung commercial displays using the MDC binary protocol. Covers Smart Signage, The Wall, LED, and SMART Signage Platform series. One connection can address several displays daisy-chained by Set ID — each appears as a display child entity.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display (or the chain's master) to the network.
2. Enable MDC / network control in the display's settings.
3. Default port is 1515.
4. In the display's menu, give each display a unique Set ID (ID). List those IDs in 'Display Set IDs' — e.g. 1 for a single display, or 1,2,3,4 for a four-panel wall.
5. Route commands to a display by picking it from the Display dropdown; use All Displays On / Off to drive the whole chain at once.

drivers.name: Sanyo / EIKI / Boxlight Projector (RS-232 Serial)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sanyo-built projectors that use Sanyo's "Basic Serial Command" RS-232 protocol: Sanyo PLC, EIKI EK / LC, and Boxlight (Eco / Boston / ProjectoWrite) lines. Works on a direct serial port or through a serial bridge. Power, input select, blank, freeze, image modes, audio, zoom, keystone, on-screen navigation, and power management, with polled power / input / lamp-hours / temperature / model status. Baud and cable type vary by model (commonly 19200; both configurable).

help.overview: EIKI EK-series projector over RS-232 (the compact "C-command" protocol: "C" + a 2-character code + carriage return). Works on a direct serial port or through a serial bridge (choose "Through a bridge" in Connection settings and pick the bridge's RS-232 port). Power, inputs, blank, freeze, image modes, audio, zoom, keystone, navigation, power management, and polled status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector's RS-232 port (or wire it to a serial bridge)
   with an RS-232 CROSS (null-modem) cable.
2. Serial settings are 19200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit,
   no flow control.
3. Through a bridge, the binding's 19200 8N1 is applied to the line
   automatically.
help.connection: The protocol requires a crossover (null-modem) cable between the controller/bridge and the projector. Status reads return on/standby, current input, lamp hours, internal temperatures, and the model name.

compatible_models.notes: Hardware-validated: two-way RS-232 control confirmed against an EK-307W (CR5 model read returns "Coral-EK-307W") at 19200 8N1 over a Global Cache iTach IP2SL serial bridge with a crossover cable.
EIKI EK / LC series projectors using the Sanyo Basic Serial Command protocol (same C00 / CRx command set). Verify baud and cable type per model before relying on it.
Sanyo PLC series, the origin of this "Basic Serial Command" protocol. Core power / input / status commands are shared; a few EK-era inputs here do not apply. Verify baud and cable type per model.
Boxlight (Sanyo-built) lines using the same C-command protocol. Note some Boxlight models (e.g. Eco Series) want a DIRECT cable rather than a crossover. Verify per model.

drivers.name: Sharp NEC Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sharp NEC projectors via the NEC binary control protocol over TCP. Compatible with P, PA, PE, PV, PX, ME, and M series projectors.

help.overview: Full-featured Sharp NEC projector control using the proprietary binary protocol on TCP port 7142. Power, input selection, picture/sound/OSD mute, freeze, shutter, volume, brightness, contrast, sharpness, aspect ratio, eco mode, lens control (zoom/focus/shift), lens memory presets, lamp/laser hours, filter hours, and detailed error status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network
2. Enable LAN control in the projector's network settings
3. Assign a static IP address to the projector
4. Default control port is 7142
5. This driver can coexist with PJLink (port 4352)
6. Set Standby Mode to 'Network Standby' or 'Sleep' to allow power-on via network
7. Input terminal codes vary by model — unsupported inputs are rejected gracefully

compatible_models.notes: Verified on hardware.
Per NEC protocol manual. Specific models like NP-P506QL fall under P series.

drivers.name: Shure Networked Devices
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Shure networked audio devices over TCP (port 2202). Covers MXA910/920/710 ceiling microphone arrays, ANI interfaces, P300 IntelliMix processor, and SCM820 automixer.

drivers.name: Philips Hue Bridge
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Philips Hue lights, rooms, zones, and scenes via the local REST API V1 on a Hue Bridge (HTTP, port 80). Every light and group is a child entity with live state; pair with the bridge's link button straight from the device page.

help.overview:
Philips Hue is the most widely deployed residential and small-commercial smart-lighting platform. The bridge sits on the LAN and bridges Zigbee bulbs / fixtures to a local REST API. AV integrators commonly use it for accent lighting in boardrooms, hospitality spaces, and houses of worship — recall a "Presentation" scene when the projector turns on, fade up "Q&A" lighting when the session ends.

Every light and every group (room / zone, plus the special "all lights" group 0) appears as a child entity with live on/brightness/color state, so bindings, macros, and triggers can react to individual lights. Scenes are offered in a picker on the recall commands.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the Hue Bridge in your router. The bridge is also discoverable via mDNS.
2. Add the device with the bridge's IP address, leaving the App Key blank.
3. Press the round link button on top of the bridge, then run the "Pair with Bridge (Link Button)" action from this device's page within 30 seconds. It requests an app key, saves it, and reconnects automatically.
4. Lights, groups, and scenes are enumerated on connect. Use "Refresh from Device" (or the refresh command) after adding fixtures in the Hue app.
5. Commands that act on a light or group offer a picker of the discovered children; scene commands offer a scene picker.

compatible_models.notes: Verified against a BSB002 bridge (API 1.77.0): discovery probe, link-button pairing wizard, light/group/scene enumeration, and control. The V2 bridge also supports the V2 / CLIP V2 API over HTTPS — this driver targets V1 only.
Exposes the same V1 REST API on port 80. End-of-life for new firmware but still functional.

drivers.name: Sonos Speaker
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sonos speakers via the local UPnP API. Play/pause, volume, mute, track info, and transport control.

help.overview: Controls any Sonos speaker on the local network via UPnP. Works with all Sonos models including One, Five, Beam, Arc, Era, Move, Roam, Port, Amp, and legacy Play/Connect models. No cloud account or API key required.
help.setup:
1. Ensure the Sonos speaker is on the same network
2. Enter the speaker's IP address (find it in the Sonos app under Settings > System > About)
3. Default port is 1400 (do not change)
4. UPnP control must be enabled on the speaker (on by default)

compatible_models.notes: UPnP API stable across all Sonos models.

drivers.name: Sony Bravia Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sony Bravia TVs and professional displays via the JSON-RPC REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Power, input, volume, mute, navigation, media transport, app launch. Covers Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia models.

help.overview: Controls Sony Bravia displays using the built-in REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Works with Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia series from ~2013 onwards (W, X, Z, A, XR models).
help.setup:
1. Connect the TV to the network.
2. On the TV, go to Settings > Network > Home Network Setup > IP Control.
3. Set Authentication to 'Normal and Pre-Shared Key'.
4. Set a Pre-Shared Key (e.g., '1234').
5. Set Simple IP Control to 'On' (enables power-on over network).
6. Enter the TV's IP address and PSK in the driver config.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on production hardware.

drivers.name: Sony VISCA-IP PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Dedicated Sony SRG / BRC / EVI VISCA-over-IP driver (UDP port 52381). Adds Sony picture profiles, R/B gain, color matrix, defog, visibility enhancer, low-light, chroma suppress, PRESET MODE + PTZ TRACE (BRC-X400/X401), tally, IR correction, ICR, AF mode, AE speed, min/max shutter, high sensitivity, and OSD on/off — on top of the standard PTZ + AE/WB command set.

help.overview: Sony PTZ camera control over VISCA-IP (UDP 52381). Includes Sony's own picture profiles, color matrix, PRESET MODE / PTZ TRACE (BRC-X400/X401), tally, OSD, AF mode, AE speed, IR correction, ICR, and shutter limits.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and put it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. Enable VISCA over IP in the camera's network menu. The default port 52381 should not need to change.
3. Confirm the camera is set to UDP — not TCP. Sony BRC/SRG cameras default to UDP; this driver speaks UDP only.
4. VISCA over IP supports up to 5 simultaneous controllers per camera, so OpenAVC can co-exist with hardware joysticks or other control surfaces.
5. Picture-profile / color-matrix / defog / PRESET MODE commands only take effect on the BRC-X400/X401 — on smaller SRG models the camera silently rejects them.

compatible_models.notes: BRC-X400 / X401 expose the full feature set (picture profiles, color matrix, defog, PRESET MODE, PTZ TRACE, tally). SRG-X400/X402/201M2 and SRG-X120/HD1M2 share the picture profile / R-B gain / chroma suppress / IR correction surface but lack PRESET MODE, PTZ TRACE, tally, color matrix and defog (commands return error harmlessly). BRC-H800 / H900 are older but speak the same Command List wire format.

drivers.name: Sony VPL Projector (ADCP)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sony VPL professional installation projectors over Sony's Advanced Display Control Protocol (ADCP) on TCP port 53595. Power, input, blank, freeze, picture mode, aspect ratio, image-quality (contrast / brightness / colour / sharpness), and the universal remote-key set. Supports SHA-256 challenge-response authentication so the projector can keep its default auth-on web setting.

help.overview: ADCP is Sony's text-based control protocol for professional VPL projectors. It runs on TCP 53595 with optional SHA-256 challenge-response authentication. The driver covers the universal command surface (power, input, blank, freeze, picture mode, image quality, aspect, remote keys) and surfaces the projector's reported power and error state.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network via its LAN or HDBaseT terminal and assign it a static IP.
2. In the projector's main menu, set Standby Mode = Standard so the projector responds to network commands while powered down.
3. Open the projector's web setup page. The default ADCP password is ``Projector`` — change it to something private.
4. In OpenAVC, enter the projector's IP and the ADCP password. Leave port at 53595.

compatible_models.notes: ADCP is the same on every VPL professional / installation projector — the command surface is consistent, the variation is which inputs and picture modes a given chassis exposes. The driver lets the user pick from the union of all inputs / modes; unsupported values return err_val on the projector, which the driver logs but does not raise.

drivers.name: vMix
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls vMix video production software via the TCP API. Supports transitions, input switching, audio, overlays, recording, streaming, titles, replay, and PTZ.

help.overview: Full control of vMix video production software. Supports input switching, transitions, audio mixing, overlays, recording/streaming, titles, replay, and PTZ cameras.
help.setup:
1. Open vMix and go to Settings > Web Controller
2. Ensure the TCP API is enabled (default port 8099)
3. Enter the vMix PC's IP address and port below
4. Tally subscription is enabled by default for real-time program/preview tracking

compatible_models.notes: Any vMix edition. Requires TCP API enabled in vMix settings.

drivers.name: Symetrix Composer DSP
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Symetrix Edge, Radius, Radius AEC, Radius NX, Prism, Solus NX, and xControl DSPs via the Composer Control Protocol on TCP port 48631. Generic controller model: assign controller numbers (1–10000) in Composer to faders, mutes, selectors, and meters; this driver reads / writes those numbers and subscribes to push-enabled value changes.

help.overview: Symetrix DSPs use a generic external-control model: the AV integrator wires controller numbers to specific DSP elements in Composer (Tools → Controller Manager) with the 'Enable Push' setting active. This driver speaks that protocol, so macros can move controllers, recall presets, and react to DSP state changes without writing custom protocol code.
help.setup:
1. In Composer, open Tools → Controller Manager and assign controller numbers (1–10000) to the faders, mutes, selectors, and meters you want to control from OpenAVC. Make sure the 'Push' checkbox is enabled for each.
2. Compile and push the design to the unit.
3. Note the unit's IP address (System Manager).
4. Enter the IP, port 48631, and num_controllers (set to the highest controller number you assigned, rounded up — default 64 covers most installations) in the device config in OpenAVC.
5. Connect. The driver enables global push and issues Push Refresh on connect, so all current values populate immediately.

compatible_models.notes: Every Symetrix DSP that runs Composer 3.0+ shares the same Control Protocol on TCP 48631. Newer NX models require Composer 6.0+. The driver's controller-number coverage is bounded only by the configured num_controllers value (default 64, max 256).

drivers.name: TOA 9000M2 Matrix Mixer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the TOA M-9000M2 Digital Matrix Mixer and protocol-compatible A-9000M2 Series mixer/amplifiers over RS-232C. 8 mixing inputs x 8 outputs: input/output fader gain, the 8x8 crosspoint matrix, channel on/off, tone, parametric EQ, loudness, HPF/LPF, input sensitivity, phantom power, preset / paging-event recall, speaker presets, and ANC. The device is write-then-echo with no live readback except channel names and ANC reference, so state is tracked optimistically from the confirmations it returns.

help.overview:
The TOA 9000M2 Series speaks a compact binary RS-232C protocol: every message is <command byte> <length> <data...>. This driver exposes the full control surface for the 8x8 matrix mixer -- faders, the crosspoint matrix, mutes, tone, parametric EQ, filters, loudness, input sensitivity, phantom power, presets, paging events, speaker presets, and ANC.

IMPORTANT -- feedback is limited. The hardware confirms each command by echoing it back, so the driver knows a change was accepted and mirrors it in state. But the protocol has NO way to read most current values back; the only true reads are channel names and the ANC reference level. As a result, changes made at the unit's front panel or by a scene recall will not appear in OpenAVC. Drive the mixer entirely from OpenAVC (or re-send known values on connect) for state to stay accurate. Fader 'nudge' commands are the exception -- the device returns the resulting level, which is read back exactly.
help.setup:
1. Wire RS-232C to the unit's D-sub 9-pin port with a STRAIGHT cable (pin 2 = TX, pin 3 = RX, pin 5 = GND).
2. Set the serial port path in the device config (e.g. COM3 on Windows, /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux) and pick the baud rate that matches the unit (9600 / 19200 / 38400 / 57600; 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit).
3. To route the mixer over the network, connect it to an IP-to-serial bridge (e.g. Global Cache iTach) and bind this device to the bridge's serial port -- OpenAVC carries the bytes through transparently.

Commands cannot be received while the unit is powered off (send Power On first).

compatible_models.notes: Digital Matrix Mixer. 8 mic/line inputs x 8 outputs. RS-232C, D-sub 9-pin, 9600-57600 8N1, straight cable.
9000M2 Series mixer/amplifiers share this RS-232C protocol. Power, phantom, and speaker-preset commands are most relevant to these amp models.

drivers.name: TurtleAV Chazy Control
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls a TurtleAV Chazy Control AV-over-IP matrix controller and the sub-units it manages: video encoders (TX), decoders (RX), and video walls. The standard Control's command set; for the Media Player, Groups, Events, Scheduler, Dante Presets, Configuration Presets and Date/Time modules, use the Chazy Control Pro driver.

help.overview: The Chazy Control orchestrates a Chazy 4K AV-over-IP system. Add it as one device; its encoders, decoders and video walls appear as child entities under the Child Entities tab. For Pro-only modules (media, groups, events, schedules, presets), use the Chazy Control Pro driver instead.
help.setup:
1. Connect the controller's Control LAN to your network. The default address is 192.168.6.100; it also advertises as controller.local.
2. Telnet on port 23 is enabled by default with no login.
3. Enter the controller's IP in the device config; leave the port at 23.
4. Encoders and decoders are discovered automatically on connect from GET STATUS. Use the Search command to find new TX/RX on the Video LAN, then Add Auto All to register them.

compatible_models.notes: Adapted from the hardware-validated Control Pro driver; the standard Control API is a documented strict subset (Chazy Control API reference, FW 1.00.17). Not yet validated against a standalone Control unit.

drivers.name: TurtleAV Chazy Control Pro
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls a TurtleAV Chazy Control Pro AV-over-IP matrix controller and every sub-unit it manages: video encoders (TX) and decoders (RX), video walls, decoder groups, events, schedules, NAS/FTP media sources, Dante presets, and configuration presets.

help.overview: The Chazy Control Pro orchestrates an entire Chazy 4K AV-over-IP system. Add it as one device; its encoders, decoders, video walls, groups, events, schedules, media sources, Dante presets, and configuration presets appear as child entities under the Child Entities tab.
help.setup:
1. Connect the controller's Control LAN (LAN2) to your network. The default address is 192.168.6.100; it also advertises as controller.local.
2. Telnet on port 23 is enabled by default with no login.
3. Enter the controller's IP in the device config; leave the port at 23.
4. Encoders and decoders are discovered automatically on connect from GET STATUS. Use 'Find + Add All Devices' to search the Video LAN and enroll everything new in one step (or Search, then Add All New Devices, to do it in stages).
5. Video walls, groups, events, and Dante presets already configured on the controller are also listed automatically. Media sources, schedules, and configuration presets cannot be listed by the controller, so they appear only once you create them here.

compatible_models.notes: Telnet API confirmed against FW 1.10.11.

drivers.name: TurtleAV Darwin Control
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls a TurtleAV Darwin Control (CTL100AL) H.265 AV-over-IP matrix controller and every sub-unit it manages: video encoders (TX), decoders (RX), and video walls.

help.overview: The Darwin Control orchestrates an entire Darwin HD AV-over-IP system. Add it as one device; its encoders, decoders, and video walls appear as child entities under the Child Entities tab.
help.setup:
1. Connect the controller's Control LAN (LAN2) to your network. The default address is 192.168.6.100; it also advertises as controller.local.
2. Telnet on port 23 is enabled by default with no login.
3. Enter the controller's IP in the device config; leave the port at 23.
4. Encoders and decoders are discovered automatically on connect from GET STATUS. Use the Search command to find new TX/RX on the Video LAN, then Add Auto All to register them.
5. Video walls already configured on the controller are also listed automatically.

compatible_models.notes: Verified end-to-end against live hardware (FW 1.50.02) with a live HDMI source on the TX and a display on the RX: connect, discovery, child enumeration, status parsing, enrolment/idempotency, and the operational SET surface (routing, output/mute/pause/OSD/auto, resolution, rotate, no-signal standby, HDCP/Osp SNK/SRC/OFF/H14/H22, TX encoding, LED/FPLED, audio input, IR, GPIO). OSD, mute, pause, resolution, rotation, output on/off, and a single-RX video wall tile were confirmed rendering on the attached display; the source-binding commands (video-wall class/matrix source, KVM hotkey) were accepted with a live source. Decoder video-wall mode (MODE VW) requires the RX assigned to a wall with an applied class region first. Only reboot/reset/network commands were held back on the live unit; their wire formats match the manufacturer reference. Multi-endpoint routing and multi-screen walls need additional TX/RX units to exercise.

drivers.name: Vaddio RoboSHOT / ConferenceShot
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Vaddio (Legrand AV) RoboSHOT and ConferenceShot PTZ cameras via the Telnet Serial Command API on port 23. Covers pan/tilt/zoom, focus, 16 presets with Tri-Synchronous Motion, CCU (color / iris / gain / detail / white-balance) controls, factory & custom CCU scenes, and standby. One driver covers the entire RoboSHOT family — HDBT, HD-SDI, NDI, IW, USB.

help.overview: The Vaddio (Legrand AV) RoboSHOT family is one of the most widely deployed PTZ camera lines in commercial AV — boardrooms, lecture capture, courtrooms, broadcast. The Telnet Serial Command API on port 23 lets external controllers drive pan/tilt/zoom, recall the 16 onboard presets (with optional Tri-Synchronous Motion for cinematic moves), tweak iris / gain / white balance, and put the camera in standby. The same commands work across every RoboSHOT and ConferenceShot model.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the camera in its web interface, or set a
   DHCP reservation in your router.
2. In the camera's web interface, on the Security page, confirm
   (or change) the admin password. The default is "password" —
   Vaddio strongly recommends changing it.
3. Enter the camera's IP address, the username (default `admin`),
   and the password below. Telnet sessions reuse the same admin
   credentials as the web UI.
4. Pan / tilt / zoom commands are drive-style — they keep moving
   until you send the matching stop. Use the per-axis "stop"
   commands or the per-axis variable-speed drive commands with
   speed=0 to halt.
5. The 16 pan/tilt/zoom presets (camera preset recall N) are
   saved in the camera. Use Tri-Synchronous Motion (the optional
   `tri-sync` speed parameter on store) for smooth simultaneous
   pan/tilt/zoom moves between presets.
6. CCU (color / lighting) values follow Vaddio's documented ranges:
   iris 0-11, gain 0-11, detail 0-15, chroma 0-14, red_gain and
   blue_gain 0-255. red/blue gain are only writable when auto white
   balance is off; iris and gain are only writable when auto-iris
   is off; backlight compensation conflicts with wide dynamic range.

compatible_models.notes: The full RoboSHOT family shares one Telnet API. Vaddio is now part of Legrand AV — older boxes still ship as "Vaddio". ConferenceShot models predate the rename and use an older firmware revision but the same command shape. Speed ranges (pan 1-24, tilt 1-20, zoom 1-7, focus 1-8) and CCU value ranges are consistent across the family.

drivers.name: WattBox IP-Controlled PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls SnapAV WattBox IP-controlled power distribution units over the WattBox Integration Protocol (Telnet, port 23). Outlets are addressable children with per-outlet state, name, and power metering. Supports on/off/toggle/reset, per-outlet naming, auto-reboot configuration, system + per-outlet power metering, and UPS status reporting on units with a connected UPS.

help.overview: WattBox is the SnapAV / Snap One family of IP-controlled power distribution units commonly installed in commercial AV racks. This driver speaks the v1.7 Integration Protocol, letting macros switch outlets on / off / reset, rename outlets, configure auto-reboot, and read live power / UPS telemetry. Use this driver instead of OvrC for local OpenAVC control — OvrC is a separate cloud product.
help.setup:
1. Connect the WattBox to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the WattBox's IP from the front panel (where applicable) or from the WattBox web interface.
3. In the WattBox web interface, ensure the integration protocol is enabled and confirm the admin username and password.
4. Enter the IP, port 23, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC.
5. Outlets are 1-indexed in commands. Use Reset All Outlets to power-cycle the whole unit.

compatible_models.notes: All current IP / IPV / IPVM WattBoxes share the v1.7 Integration Protocol. Outlets are reconciled from the unit's reported outlet count, so 3 / 12 / 18-outlet models each surface exactly their outlets as children.

drivers.name: Yamaha MTX/MRX/XMV
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Yamaha install-audio processors (MTX3, MTX5-D, MRX7-D) and the XMV power amps + EXi8 / EXo8 audio expanders over the Remote Control Protocol (RCP) on TCP port 49280. Push-capable: NOTIFY messages from the device drive state immediately; polling backstops refresh and a liveness watchdog detects a silently dead link. MRX7-D parameters are addressed via Remote Control Setup List Index numbers (1..32); MTX/XMV use full parameter paths via generic set_param / get_param.

help.overview:
Yamaha RCP is the unified ASCII control protocol used across the MTX, MRX, XMV, EXi8, and EXo8 product family. The protocol is push-capable - the device sends a NOTIFY message whenever a parameter changes, whether from this controller, the front panel, another remote controller, or a preset/snapshot recall.
For MRX7-D, integrators define a Remote Control Setup List in MTX-MRX Editor that maps each panel control (fader, mute, selector) to an Index number. This driver exposes 32 Index slots; bind your panel UI to the set_index / inc_index / query_index commands.
For MTX3 / MTX5-D / XMV / EXi8 / EXo8, addresses look like MTX:mem_512/60000/0/0/0/0/0 - the seven-element path identifies a specific channel/parameter. Look up addresses in section 7 ("Parameter List") of the RCP specification, then use set_param / get_param / inc_param.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Yamaha device(s) to the network via Ethernet. 2. In MTX-MRX Editor (or ProVisionaire Edit for newer firmware), open
   System -> Remote Control. Enable network remote control on TCP port
   49280. The device supports up to 8 simultaneous remote sessions.
3. (MRX7-D only) In MTX-MRX Editor, open Remote Control Setup List.
   Assign each panel control to an Index number 1..32. Synchronize the
   project to the device.
4. Enter the device's IP address in the OpenAVC device config. Leave
   port at 49280.
5. Optional: set keepalive_timeout > 0 to enable RCP keepalive for
   unreliable networks. The device will drop the connection if no
   command arrives within the configured timeout.

compatible_models.notes: Matrix processors. MRX7-D requires a Remote Control Setup List in MTX-MRX Editor that maps user faders / mutes / selectors to Index numbers; this driver controls them by Index. MTX3 / MTX5-D use full parameter addresses via the generic set_param command.
XMV power amps. Controlled via full parameter paths (set_param / get_param). RCP control is independent of any MTX/MRX in the system.
Audio I/O expanders. Same RCP address model as XMV.
